body.objective: Determine whether the complex-compensator extension has a global or topological gauge anomaly on its first declared compact backgrounds, rather than inferring global consistency from vanishing local anomaly cohomology.
body.stop_condition: Import the terminal complex-compensator classical BV parent and the all-loop local tau-adic QME disposition by exact hashes. Declare the actual diffeomorphism, Weyl and internal-phase gauge groups, their connected components, the field-space and bundle sectors, the Euclidean continuations used, and the fermionic/bosonic determinant or Pfaffian line whose holonomy would define a global anomaly. On the vacuum-cylinder continuation and the first admissible Berger continuation, classify the relevant large gauge transformations and mapping tori. Compute, with two independent rails where a finite invariant exists, every applicable determinant-line holonomy, eta/mod-two index, cobordism or group-cohomology obstruction. Prove vanishing, exhibit a nontrivial phase, or certify the first precise non-definition caused by a missing elliptic family, regulator, orientation or global field-space construction. Export a machine-readable global-anomaly ledger linked to the local QME result, mutations that alter one large transformation or bundle sector, and a report that states exactly which topology and field content were covered.
body.current_gate: global-anomaly disposition for the changed complex-compensator theory on the first compact laboratories
body.forbid: no H^{1,4}(s|d)=0 used as proof of global anomaly freedom; no background partition-function phase called a determinant-line theorem; no Lorentzian causal claim inferred from a Euclidean mapping torus; no single connected gauge component called the full gauge group; no strict pure-Weyl conclusion imported from the changed compensator complex; no positivity, particles, scattering, unitarity or all-background quantum-gravity claim
activates: a global quantum-consistency boundary for the compensator extension
body.resource_hint: LATE COMPENSATOR GATE. Begin only after the local all-loop and classical global-field-content inputs are terminal. A certified non-definition is preferable to treating local BRST cohomology as a global theorem.
notes: This gate separates perturbative local anomaly cancellation from topology-sensitive phases under large transformations.
The first scope is deliberately limited to the declared compact cylinder and Berger continuations and their actual bundle sectors.
If the theory contains no fermionic Pfaffian, the remaining determinant-line and measure phases must still be classified rather than assumed absent.
